question: Why is giving a patient a regular bath or helping them wash up so important in the ward?

options.A: It prevents skin breakdown and infections
options.B: It helps the patient get discharged faster
options.C: It stops doctors from doing morning rounds

explanation: You're doing great! Regular hygiene washes away harmful germs and dead skin cells, keeping pressure sores and infections far away from your patient. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h1)

question: When you help a patient with their personal hygiene, why is it considered a special nursing care rather than just a normal house chore?

options.A: It replaces the need to give prescribed drugs
options.B: It is the only duty a nurse can leave for relatives
options.C: It allows the nurse to assess the skin and build trust
options.D: It guarantees the patient will feel zero pain

explanation: Spot on! Washing and grooming put you close enough to spot early skin changes and build a warm, trusting relationship with your patient. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h1)

question: When giving a bed bath, which direction should you always wash the patient's body?

options.A: From the legs up straight to the face
options.B: From the sides toward the back spine
options.C: From the most sensitive parts to the least sensitive
options.D: From the cleanest areas to the dirtiest areas

explanation: Brilliant! Always start with the cleanest parts (like the face) and move down so you don't drag dirt and germs onto clean skin. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h2)

question: You just finished giving an elderly patient a bed bath. How should you dry their skin safely?

options.A: Rub their skin hard to wake up blood flow
options.B: Pat the skin dry gently with a soft towel
options.C: Put thick lotion tightly between their toes
options.D: Use a hair dryer on high heat to dry them quickly

explanation: Spot on! Older skin is quite fragile. Always pat gently with a soft towel instead of scrubbing, which can tear the skin. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h2)

question: Poor mouth care in bedridden patients can lead to which serious lung problem?
explanation: You've got this! Germs hiding in an uncleaned mouth can easily slip down into the lungs and cause a dangerous infection called aspiration pneumonia. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h3)

question: Why must an unconscious patient be turned to their side when you are cleaning their mouth?

options.A: To prevent liquids from entering the airway and causing choking
options.B: To stop them from rolling off the bed
options.C: To increase blood flow to the facial nerves
options.D: To make it easier to brush the back teeth

explanation: Awesome! Turning them to the side lets water and saliva pool in the cheek and run out safely, rather than choking their airway. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h3)

question: Why must a nurse be extra careful when cutting the nails of a patient with diabetes?

options.A: Clipping nails makes blood sugar shoot up instantly
options.B: Decreased sensation means minor injuries can go unnoticed and lead to severe ulcers
options.C: Special clippers for diabetics can shock them
options.D: Diabetic nails grow much faster than normal

explanation: Good job! Diabetes can damage nerve feelings in the feet, meaning a small cut can turn into a serious, hidden ulcer very quickly. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a safe thing to do when giving a patient nail care?

options.A: Washing the feet with warm water
options.B: Rounding down the deep corners of toenails
options.D: Inspecting the skin between the toes

explanation: You're learning fast! Never round the corners of toenails too deep—it makes them grow painfully right into the skin (ingrown nails). [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h4)

question: What is the correct way to wipe when cleaning a female patient's private parts (perineal care)?

options.A: From the pubic area toward the anus
options.B: From the anus toward the tummy

explanation: Correct! Always wipe front-to-back. This keeps germs from the back passage away from the urinary opening, stopping nasty infections. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h5)

question: What happens if a nurse forgets to push the foreskin back down after cleaning an uncircumcised male patient?

options.A: Paraphimosis and painful swelling of the penis
options.D: A fast fungal infection on the legs

explanation: Spot on! Leaving the foreskin pulled back acts like a tight rope, cutting off blood flow and causing a painful swelling called paraphimosis. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h5)

question: In nursing, what does the term 'self-care deficit' mean?

options.A: An impaired ability to perform daily activities like bathing and grooming
options.B: Lacking school training on health habits
options.C: Not having enough money to buy soap
options.D: A patient refusing help from any health worker

explanation: You got this! A self-care deficit simply means a patient struggles to do daily tasks like washing or dressing on their own. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h6)

question: A stroke patient has weak arms on one side, but she can still wash her face if her wash basin is placed close by. What should you do?

options.A: Tell her family to do all her bathing when they visit
options.B: Wait until her full strength returns before she bathes
options.C: Encourage her to wash her upper body while you assist with the rest
options.D: Do everything for her to save her energy

explanation: Wonderful choice! Encouraging whatever independence a patient has left boosts their mood and helps them recover faster. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h6)

question: When should you change your basin water and washcloth during a bed bath?

options.A: Only after the whole body wash is finished
options.B: Every fifteen minutes sharp on the clock
options.C: Whenever a visitor walks into the room
options.D: When the water becomes cool, soapy, or visibly dirty

explanation: Exactly! Changing dirty or cold water keeps you from spreading germs back onto the parts of the body you just cleaned. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h7)

question: What is the proper thing to do with dirty bedsheets right after removing them from a patient's bed?

options.A: Fold them nicely and put them on the patient's bedside table
options.B: Place them directly into a designated laundry hamper
options.C: Drop them on the floor until you finish your shift
options.D: Spread them across a clean chair for later

explanation: Spot on! Putting dirty linens straight into the laundry basket stops germs from spreading around the ward and keeps tables clean. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h7)

question: How can you best protect a patient's dignity and privacy when giving them a bed bath?

options.A: By keeping completely silent so they don't feel awkward
options.B: By asking all family members to stay outside forever
options.C: By opening the ward windows wide for fresh air
options.D: By keeping the patient covered with a sheet and exposing only the area being washed

explanation: Brilliant! Strategic draping with a bedsheet keeps your patient covered, warm, and feeling respected while you work. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h8)

question: A patient says they prefer taking their bath in the evening right before sleep, instead of the morning. What should you do?

options.A: Insist that morning baths are the only way to stop skin sores
options.B: Adjust the routine to accommodate the patient's personal preference
options.C: Tell them hospital rules say baths must happen before breakfast
options.D: Refuse because evening shifts are too busy

explanation: You're a star! Whenever it's clinically safe, always respect your patient's personal routine to make them feel at home in the hospital. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h8)
